response.evidence: Out of 56 applications from non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64 in the dataset, 51 were approved (an approval rate of approximately 91%). The small number of denied applications typically exhibit risk factors such as very high loan-to-value ratios (e.g., 100%) or high debt-to-income ratios (e.g., 50%-60%), indicating decisions are based on financial metrics rather than demographic discrimination.

The data shows a high approval rate for non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64, including approvals for individuals with high debt-to-income (DTI) ratios (up to 49%) and high loan-to-value (LTV) ratios (up to 100%). Denials within this group are primarily linked to high-risk financial factors, such as DTI ratios exceeding 50%. Similar approval standards and occasional denials for otherwise strong financial profiles appear consistently across other demographics, indicating that loan decisions are driven by financial criteria rather than demographic bias.

The dataset indicates a very high loan origination rate for non-Hispanic White females aged 55-64. The limited number of denied applications for this specific demographic consistently correlate with high debt-to-income ratios (such as 50%-60% and >60%), which is a standard financial risk factor for denial applied across all applicant groups rather than evidence of demographic discrimination.
